old: “I bring back only what is useful now. The rest can remain safely held until there is more capacity. I return to the room, the body, the day, and one honest action. All instructions to deepen or remain in this session are finished. I keep only the ordinary-life intention or future-practice cue I consciously chose; neither keeps today’s altered state running. I am myself, in my body, with adult judgment fully available.”
new: Bring back to yourself only what will be of use to yourself in the present moment and leave the rest for another time. Slowly return to being in body and in this place, back into normal day to day living. The session is over. There are no more instructions to follow, nothing to do except to go back to the life that led up to this point. If there is an intention to bring something into ordinary life or to do something in the future, these are simply cues, and do not continue the altered state.

old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.
new: What if you are using a recording and it stops before it lets you out? Don’t sit there waiting for the voice to come back and release you. Say to yourself, “the recording has stopped and the session is over.” Then use the above method to get out. Start by opening your eyes, saying where you are, saying what day it is, pushing down with your feet or your hands, moving about, looking around, etc. Then go through the 5 step method.

old: Sleep is separate. A sleep recording may end in sleep or quiet rest. A waking recording shouldn’t end by preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, an undefined reset word, or an invitation to remain altered indefinitely.
new: Note: It is all right to use a recording to help you go to sleep. However, a recording for use when you are awake should not leave you in a role, with lowered judgement, impaired movement capabilities, blank, with an undefined reset word, invited to stay altered indefinitely, etc.

old: “Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
new: Can you show me a single sensation in the body? Can you show me a single word? Can you show me how you know whether to listen or rest today?

old: First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform. Not experiencing an inner voice or image isn’t, by itself, resistance or a missing adult capacity. Correct an explicitly unwanted invitation. If you recognize a protective part, you can talk to it:
new: Do you know what is fake? Just because you don't have an inner voice/image doing this, it doesn't mean you are being a child or resisting doing the work. If you feel that something is asking you to do something that you do not want to do, then correct it. If you feel that a part might be protecting you from this, then talk to it.

old: The fake feeling can also mean that a needed adult capacity isn’t available yet. Stop demanding a convincing voice. If you can already observe what is happening, borrow the particular warmth, boundary, or direction you lack. A real or imagined caring figure can help. Try one believable sentence or action and see how it is received.
new: If it is not there, stop trying to believe an inner voice. If you have enough observing ego, borrow whatever you need - warmth, boundary, direction etc - from someone who you can imagine is good enough, maybe a family member, a friend or a famous person. Try out something which rings true, a sentence, an action etc and see how it goes.

old: Conscious agreement is one thing. Unconscious receptivity is another. Emotional compliance is another. Legal and ethical consent is another. A mind can be influenced without the adult self having clearly chosen the influence.
new: Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent. Can people have their minds influenced without conscious agreement of their adult self?
